title_en: Liu Benyuan v. Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau — administrative dispute over decision on infringement of property rights and operational autonomy

full_text_en:
Liu Benyuan v. Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau — Administrative Dispute over Infringement of Property Rights and Autonomous Management Rights

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Liu Benyuan, male, 51 years old, factory director of Chengdu Pujiang Berberine Factory, former Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory, and Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory.

Agent ad litem: Wu Chuanyu, lawyer at Chengdu Dazhong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yan Xiaochuan, lawyer at Chengdu Dazhong Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Zhou Shangwu, Director.

Agent ad litem: Xu Chengyao, lawyer at Pujiang County Law Firm.

Appellant Liu Benyuan, dissatisfied with the administrative judgment of the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province in the administrative litigation case concerning Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau's infringement of property rights and autonomous management rights, appealed to the Sichuan High People's Court. After public trial, the court found the following facts:

In May 1983, Appellant Liu Benyuan invested 24,000 yuan, and Li and An each invested 8,000 yuan, to jointly establish Pujiang County Shou'an Berberine Factory. The business license issued by the Pujiang County Administration for Industry and Commerce recorded the economic nature as "collective (joint venture of specialized households)." At the end of the same year, Li and An withdrew from the partnership, and the factory was thereafter operated solely by Liu Benyuan. On October 8, 1984, Liu Benyuan signed the "Agreement on Transfer of Property" with the Pujiang County Agricultural Machinery Bureau, whereby the Pujiang County Agricultural Machinery Bureau transferred its former agricultural machinery school property of 2,403 square meters to Pujiang County Shou'an Berberine Factory for 29,000 yuan. In April 1991, Liu Benyuan obtained the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" and the "Chengdu Construction Land Permit."

On December 22, 1984, Appellant Liu Benyuan applied to the Pujiang County Science and Technology Committee for approval to establish Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory. The committee approved the application and decided that the factory would be under its leadership. On April 15, 1985, the Pujiang County Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a business license to Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory, stating the economic nature as "collective." To address the printing factory's water supply issues, Liu Benyuan invested personally to drill two machine wells approximately 80 meters deep within the factory premises. Upon use, Liu discovered that one well had high-quality water, which was identified by the Sichuan Provincial Bureau of Geology and Mineral Resources as metasilicic acid natural mineral water suitable for drinking. On December 6, 1986, with the consent of the Pujiang County Science and Technology Committee, Liu Benyuan, in the name of the printing factory, jointly established Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory with Chengdu Beverage Factory, and obtained a business license. The license recorded the economic nature as "joint venture between state-owned and collective." One year later, the parties terminated the joint venture, and the beverage factory was thereafter operated by Liu Benyuan. When the business license was renewed, the economic nature of the beverage factory was changed to "collective." On September 28, 1987, the Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau issued Document No. Puxiangqi (1987) 23, placing Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory and Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory under its management.

In 1989, in accordance with the notice from the State Administration for Industry and Commerce regarding the review of individual and private enterprises holding collective business licenses, the Pujiang County Administration for Industry and Commerce required Appellant Liu Benyuan to change the economic nature of his enterprises to private. In June 1990, Liu Benyuan applied to the bureau for a change in enterprise nature, but due to the objection of the Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau, the change was not effected. In August 1991, Liu Benyuan, in the name of Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory and with the consent of the Pujiang County Mining Office and the Township Enterprise Administration Bureau, applied to the Sichuan Provincial Bureau of Geology and Mineral Resources for a mineral water mining permit. On August 30 of the same month, the Pujiang County People's Government sent a letter to the provincial bureau requesting a delay in issuing the mining permit.

On January 7, 1992, the Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau issued an appointment and removal decision: appointing Deng as the factory director of Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory and Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory, and removing Appellant Liu Benyuan from the positions of factory director of Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory and Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory. At the same time, the bureau also sealed up Chengdu Pujiang Berberine Factory, Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory, Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory, and inventory items worth approximately 100,000 yuan. The newly appointed factory director directed relevant personnel to take two refrigerated cabinets, nine aluminum alloy shelves, and four pagers from the Chengdu sales department of Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory. These actions caused the joint venture project that Liu Benyuan had signed in October 1991 with the General Manager of Thailand International Development Co., Ltd. and the Chairman of Thailand Jiancheng Enterprise Company (Wu, among others) to abort, and made it impossible for him to fulfill the repayment of loans and interest due in 1992 confirmed by Civil Mediation Documents No. (1991) 35 and No. (1991) 40 of the Pujiang County People's Court. Consequently, Liu Benyuan filed an administrative lawsuit with the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court.

On June 10, 1992, the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court commissioned the Sichuan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce to determine the economic nature of the three enterprises in this case. The bureau, through Document No. Chuangong Han (1992) 176, determined the nature of the three enterprises as private enterprises.

The Chengdu Intermediate People's Court held that the three enterprises operated by the plaintiff, Liu Benyuan, were nominally collective but actually private enterprises. The defendant's appointment and removal decision and the administrative act of sealing up property exceeded its authority and were illegal. The defendant's illegal administrative acts caused certain economic losses to Liu Benyuan. However, since the enterprises were still in production and the property had not been lost, the defendant should return the property and compensate Liu Benyuan for his economic losses during the period of his removal. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 54, Item (2), Subparagraphs 1 and 4 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the court rendered the following judgment on October 28, 1993: 1. Revoke the appointment and removal decision Puxiangqi Han (1992) No. 1 of the defendant, Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau. 2. Revoke the specific administrative act of the defendant sealing up the property of Chengdu Pujiang Berberine Factory, Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory, and Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory. 3. The defendant shall return to the plaintiff the two refrigerated cabinets, nine aluminum alloy shelves, and four pagers owned by Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory. 4. The defendant shall compensate the plaintiff for economic losses during the period of his removal in the amount of 20,000 yuan. 5. The plaintiff's other claims are dismissed.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, the plaintiff, Liu Benyuan, appealed to the Sichuan High People's Court, arguing that the three enterprises in this case were established by the appellant and requested the court of second instance to confirm that they belonged to him personally, in order to protect his lawful property ownership and autonomous management rights. He also argued that the compensation of 20,000 yuan for economic losses awarded by the court of first instance was insufficient to cover the actual losses caused by the appellee, and requested compensation of 1,000,000 yuan in economic losses and the return of property. The appellee, Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau, continued to defend on the grounds that the three enterprises were registered as collective enterprises with the Administration for Industry and Commerce and that the competent authority had the right to manage them.

The Sichuan High People's Court held upon trial: The capital for the establishment of Chengdu Pujiang Berberine Factory, Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory, and Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory was all personally invested by Appellant Liu Benyuan. The distribution form, operation, and management were actually conducted in accordance with private enterprises. According to Article 7, Paragraph 1 of the Interim Regulations on Private Enterprises of the PRC, which states that "a sole proprietorship enterprise refers to an enterprise invested and operated by one person," the above three enterprises should be considered private enterprises, and the enterprise property belongs to Liu Benyuan. The decision of the appellee, Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau, to remove Liu Benyuan from his position as factory director and appoint another person as factory director, as well as the act of sealing up the enterprise property, were specific administrative acts that exceeded the bureau's authority and lacked legal basis. These acts caused Liu Benyuan to lose actual control over his property and prevented him from organizing the enterprises' production and operation, thereby infringing upon Liu Benyuan's property ownership and the autonomous management rights of the private enterprises. Therefore, the appellee's acts were illegal specific administrative acts and should be revoked. The first instance judgment revoking the appellee's appointment and removal decision and the sealing-up act was correct and should be affirmed.

The specific administrative acts implemented by the appellee, Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau, essentially deprived Liu Benyuan of his rights to possess, use, benefit from, and dispose of the enterprise property, as well as his right to organize production and operation, and caused actual harm, infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of Appellant Liu Benyuan. The appellee should bear liability for compensation. During the trial, Liu Benyuan indicated to the Sichuan High People's Court that, considering the difficulties of the appellee, Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau, he voluntarily waived part of his compensation claims, only requesting the return of property, compensation for lost wages of himself, Luo Suqiong, Liu Hongwei, Liu Wei, Chang Baoqiang, and others, as well as the interest losses for 1992 and 1993 arising from the inability to repay the loans and interest confirmed by the Pujiang County People's Court's civil mediation documents. The Sichuan High People's Court found that the appellant's above compensation claims were well-founded and should be supported. The first instance judgment found that the appellee's acts had caused certain economic losses to Liu Benyuan but did not order the appellee to bear compensation liability; it only ordered the appellee to compensate Liu Benyuan 20,000 yuan for economic losses during the period of his removal, which was inappropriate and should be reversed. Accordingly, on January 26, 1994, pursuant to Article 61, Item (2) and Article 67, Paragraphs 1 and 3 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the court rendered the following judgment:

1. Affirm Items 1 and 2 of the administrative judgment (1992) Cheng Chu Zi No. 1 of the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province, i.e., revoke the appointment and removal decision Puxiangqi Han (1992) No. 1 issued by the Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau on January 7, 1992, and the specific administrative act of sealing up the property of Chengdu Pujiang Berberine Factory, Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory, and Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory;

2. Reverse Items 3, 4, and 5 of the administrative judgment (1992) Cheng Chu Zi No. 1 of the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province;

3. The appellee, Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau, shall return the property of Chengdu Pujiang Berberine Factory, Chengdu Chaoyang Printing Factory, and Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory, which belong to Appellant Liu Benyuan, turn over the above three enterprises to Liu Benyuan for operation and management, and return the two refrigerated cabinets, nine aluminum alloy shelves, and four pagers belonging to Appellant Liu Benyuan at the Chengdu sales department of Chengdu Heshan Mineral Water Beverage Factory;

4. The appellee, Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau, shall compensate Appellant Liu Benyuan and others for lost wages in the amount of 39,600 yuan, and for the interest (including compound interest, penalty interest, etc.) losses arising from the failure to repay the loans and interest due in 1992 as confirmed in Civil Mediation Documents No. (1991) 35 and No. (1991) 40 of the Pujiang County People's Court, from January 8, 1992, to the date this judgment takes effect, with the specific amount to be calculated based on the settlement of the lending institution;

5. Items 3 and 4 above shall be performed within 15 days after this judgment takes effect.

First and second instance litigation costs each 15,500 yuan, other litigation activity fees each 1,500 yuan, totaling 34,000 yuan, shall be borne by the appellee, Pujiang County Township Enterprise Administration Bureau.
